title: Eight-round AES-128 known-key integral tuple construction, Gilbert 2014

target.description: Eight-round AES-128 with the standard known key schedule, initial whitening and no final MixColumns, as defined in Section 2. The adversary constructs a tuple with a specified input-output relation.

setting.key_relation: One known random key; no key recovery, related-key oracle or adversarially chosen key is required.
setting.key_population: every known AES-128 key in the stated construction
setting.reference_model: A perfect random 128-bit permutation and its inverse, queried at most N=2^64 times. Proposition 4 bounds the probability of producing N pairs satisfying the same byte-uniformity relation by 1/(2^128-(N-1)), hence at most 2^-127.
assumptions: Known-key structural model of Section 3, not the ordinary secret-key PRP distinguishing game.
N=2^64 distinct inputs and their outputs; each byte position is uniformly distributed across the input tuple and across the output tuple.
Only the AES-128 instance is instantiated here; source footnote 2 also discusses extension to the other key lengths.

time.note: Section 4.1 gives T=N=2^64 AES8 computations to derive the tuple; Section 3 defines the work unit and includes checking the relation in the model. The source uses an AES-equivalent dominant-work estimate; tuple derivation and relation verification are not assumed to be identical machine operations.

data.note: Tuple order N and output size, not chosen-plaintext queries to an unknown secret-key encryption oracle.

memory.note: No explicit peak-memory count for this construction is extracted; tuple size is not silently converted to peak storage.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing resource is tabulated.

success.description: For every known key in the stated instance, Algorithm A deterministically constructs the complete source-defined tuple satisfying relation R. This is a theoretical construction guarantee, not secret-key recovery or an experimentally measured fraction. The ideal-permutation construction bound is a separate event.

review.scope: Targeted verification of Properties 1–2 and Algorithm A, the exact relation and applicable key model; the independent-key and standard-schedule targets stay separate.

components.description: Proposition 4 bounds success of an arbitrary ideal-permutation algorithm making q <= N = 2^64 queries. The displayed bound is at most 2^-127; it is not the real-AES construction success.

evidence.locator: Printed pp.203-204, Section 2, AESr convention; pp.208-210, Section 3, Definitions 1-2; pp.213-215, Section 4.1, relation R, algorithm A and Proposition 4.
evidence.interpretation: The source constructs a 2^64-pair integral relation in 2^64 AES8 computations, and separately proves a small ideal-permutation probability for the same query budget. Memory and reusable preprocessing are not inferred from tuple size.

evidence.locator: Complete PDF1–23 / printed200–222; Definitions1–2 PDF9–10; §4.1 PDF14–17; §4.2 PDF18–22; allreferences.
evidence.interpretation: Complete exact conference-version inventory. Ideal-permutation success bounds, tuple order and AES-side deterministic construction remain distinct.

evidence.locator: PDF4/printed203 footnote2; PDF14–16/printed213–215 Section4.1, Properties1–2, Algorithm A and Proposition4, including explicit independent-subkey applicability.
evidence.interpretation: Success backfill: source-proved real-cipher relation construction and ideal-world probability bound are distinct events. No new attack, resource conversion or whole-paper audit.

limitations: The known-key construction was not executed at its 2^64-tuple scale.
The source itself cites other eight-round known-key relations with lower cost; different tuple relations are not automatically comparable.
This is a structural known-key result, not an attack recovering an unknown AES key.
Bounded later-literature check identifies GR17 and its revised-description note; its full result inventory is a separate work, not a cost replacement for this relation.
